title: Experiment contracts & gating canvas (WIP)
content:
Status: draft (working canvas for cross-functional experiment contracts and gating).

Purpose
- Create a lightweight, reusable "contract" between Product, Eng, SRE, Data, and UX that defines success criteria, guardrails, and handoffs for canaries and A/B tests.
- Make the gating rules explicit so on-call and PMs know when to roll forward, pause, or rollback without ad-hoc debate.

Scope / When to use
- New model variants, infrastructure changes affecting inference path, major optimization rollouts (quantization, batching), routing changes, or UI-affecting model behavior.
- Not for purely exploratory analytics work. If user-impacting, use this canvas.

Roles & Responsibilities (contract shorthand)
- Product owner: hypothesis, primary metrics, release window, business rollback criteria.
- Eng (owner): deployment plan, canary config, safe defaults, fallback, PR link.
- SRE/Infra: capacity guardrails, throttles, emergency kill switch, runbook pointer.
- Data/Measurement: metric definitions, instrumentation, power/sample calc, alert thresholds.
- UX/CS: user messaging and support playbook if surfaced.
- Security/Compliance (if required): data access, retention limits, audit log location.

Contract template (fill before push)
- Hypothesis (one sentence): "Changing X to Y will increase metric M by >= delta in N days".
- Primary metric (metric id + owner + dashboard link).
- Secondary metrics (latency, error rate, cost per request, throughput).
- Guardrails (explicit) – e.g. "P99 latency increase > 30% AND error rate > 0.5% -> pause".
- Ramp plan: slices (internal beta -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%), time per slice, required stability window.
- Fallback behavior: automatic swap to baseline model or degraded mode. PR: paste link.
- Observability hooks: dashboard urls, traces, alert names (channel).
- Communication: who notifies on each gate decision (roles + Slack channel).

Signal taxonomy (practical)
- Commitment signals (go/no-go): primary metric delta, conversion delta, revenue delta.
- Reliability signals (hard guardrails): 5xx/sec, p95/p99 latency, mem/GPUs OOM, KV-cache misses, cost/unit.
- User-facing safety signals: hallucination rate (from eval set), toxic-content detection hits, legal flags.
- Operational cost signals: tokens per request, infra spend anomaly % vs baseline.

Gating matrix (example thresholds — adjust per experiment)
- Smoke gate (0.5–2 hours): no 5xx, p95 within +20% of baseline. If fail -> rollback immediately.
- Ramp gate (each increment): stability window 24h, primary metric not worse than -1% or trending back up within 3 checks.
- Business gate before 25%: minimum sample size calculated by Data; if not reached, pause ramp.

Canary execution checklist (prep & run)
- Preflight (2 days before): finalize contract, assign on-call, update runbook links, create experiment JIRA ticket with checklist.
- Instrumentation: validate event schemas, shadow traffic mode for metrics sanity, enable debug logs for first slice only.
- Slice config: define slice names, routing rule IDs, cookie/consent behavior.
- Automated safety controls: traffic kill switch with single click, automatic fallback route, circuit-breaker thresholds in infra.
- Observe: log sampling, latency heatmaps, session-level traces for 10 failing requests.
- Decision cadence: PM + Eng + SRE async check at 1h, 4h, 24h. Use Slack thread for recorded decisions.

Rollback decision tree (short)
- Immediate rollback: any sustained increase in 5xx or p99 spikes beyond gate; catastrophic user data exposure; non-recoverable infra faults.
- Conditional pause: degradation in primary metric beyond acceptable window but non-critical reliability issues — pause and investigate for 12–24h.
- Manual override: PM can request rollback for business reasons even within gates.

A/B specifics (statistical hygiene)
- Data team must publish sample size and power calc before ramp > 5%. Use conservative minimums when conversion is low.
- Randomization must be stable per user id (or session) and not correlated with geographic routing unless intended.
- Retention window: define how long we count an outcome (e.g., 7 days for conversion).

Observability & dashboards
- Minimum dashboards to create: primary metric timeseries, latency p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, per-slice error heatmap, cost per request.
- Tracing: sample user traces that hit new code path and baseline.
